meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: irregular mixed conjugation: бегу, бежишь, ..., бегут

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.
That's no problem.
This time there's no trick.
That's no problem at all.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.trans: Faster!
He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!
How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
Who are your rivals?
Is this your programme?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.

examples.trans: Don't worry.
I'm nervous.
Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'goal' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The team scored a beautiful goal.

examples.text: А сегодня вдруг забили три быстрых гола!
examples.trans: And today they suddenly scored three quick goals!

examples.text: Они пропустили гол на последней минуте!
examples.trans: They conceded a goal in the last minute!

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.
Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: at home, a party, or a restaurant

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.
You have visitors!

meanings.note: поставить громко = to put a phone on speaker

examples.trans: I'll put it on speaker.

examples.text: Не говорите так громко, дети спят.
examples.trans: Don't speak so loudly, the children are asleep.

examples.text: Ой, это Илона! Я громко поставлю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's Ilona! I'll put it on speaker.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'door' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Open the door.
The door is behind the wardrobe.
Open the door. Is this flat nine?
We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.
Don't wait for me.
I'm waiting for you.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's life.
I want a different life.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: a door, a shop, or a legal case

examples.trans: We will close your case.
Close the door, please.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.
Please enter the courtroom.
A big hall.
Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'game, play' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a great game!
A computer game.

examples.text: Это отличная игра! Хочешь с нами поиграть? Бери карты.
examples.trans: This is a great game! Want to play with us? Take the cards.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: I'm going home.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'potatoes' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I only eat potatoes.

examples.text: Я целый год ела только картошку.
examples.trans: I ate only potatoes for a whole year.

examples.text: Ты останешься на кухне чистить картошку.
examples.trans: You will stay in the kitchen peeling potatoes.

meanings.en: to command, be in charge, give orders
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to command, to give orders', paired with 'скомандовать'.

examples.text: Да я на всё готов! Командуйте.
examples.trans: Why, I'm ready for anything! Give the orders.
Give the orders.

examples.text: Здесь командую только я и никто больше.
examples.trans: Only I command here and no one else.
There's no need to shout.
Why are you shouting?

examples.text: Не надо кричать. Хорошо, я буду сегодня.
examples.trans: There's no need to shout. All right, I'll be there tonight.
We're sitting in the kitchen.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.
All right, here you go.
OK, I'm coming.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'only, merely' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is only an ordinary game.

examples.text: Шеф, это всего лишь обычная спортивная игра.
examples.trans: Chef, it is only an ordinary sports game.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'match, game' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A soccer match.

examples.text: Тихо, Сеня! Сейчас идёт решающий матч!
examples.trans: Quiet, Senya! A decisive match is on right now!

examples.text: Кто сегодня играет на этом матче?
examples.trans: Who is playing in this match today?

мешать.gloss: to be in the way, to disturb

meanings.en: to be in the way, to hinder

examples.trans: The radiators are in the way.
Don't bother me!

examples.text: Филиппыч, миксер проехать не может. Радиаторы мешают.
examples.trans: Filippych, the mixer truck can't get through. The radiators are in the way.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.
Just a minute!

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.
Where's my toy car?
That's mine.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

examples.text: Неужели так трудно найти хороший сюжет?
examples.trans: Is it really so difficult to find a good story?

examples.text: Неужели президент накажет вас за правду?
examples.trans: Will the president really punish you for the truth?
Do you really not care at all?
I have no money at all.
No problems at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

examples.trans: I need a job too.
Do you need a pen?
He needs money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.
When are you travelling back?

examples.text: Вот это дело! Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Now we're talking! Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.
It was an ordinary day.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.

meanings.note: playful derogatory nickname used by Chef Barinov for Max

examples.trans: Runt, are you still standing here?
The chef often called the newcomer a runt.

examples.text: Огузок, ты официально принят в штат нашего ресторана!
examples.trans: Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: They are building a centre.
History will punish them.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.
It's another trick.
Rain again.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.
I'll get out of here.
You won't leave here.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.
I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'варской'). Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('chef's, culinary').

examples.trans: The chef's hat is lying on the table.
The chef put on a chef's hat.
I will eat my chef's hat!
First and last time.
This is my last question.
I'm asking for the last time.
Why are we going so slowly?
Why are you here?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?
He brought you a dog.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: money, a game, a bet, or an election

examples.trans: I lost it on the stock exchange.
Our team lost.

examples.text: Денег нет, Самсон. Я их на бирже проиграл.
examples.trans: There is no money, Samson. I lost it on the stock exchange.

meanings.en: to let through, allow to pass
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'пустить'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to let through, pass'.

examples.trans: Let us through forward quickly.

examples.text: Слышишь, братан, пропусти нас скорее вперёд.
examples.trans: Listen, bro, let us through forward quickly.

examples.text: Этот инспектор не пропустит ни одной ошибки.
examples.trans: This inspector won't miss a single mistake.
I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.trans: Let them build.
Let him come.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.
I'll do it myself.
He knows himself.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.
I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?
Understood, chef!
Understood, chef! I will find the knife.

examples.text: Слушаюсь, шеф, я сделаю всё моментально.
examples.trans: Understood, chef, I will do everything instantly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'портивный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sports, athletic').

examples.trans: That was an interesting sports game.

examples.text: Шеф, это всего лишь обычная спортивная игра.
examples.trans: Chef, it is only an ordinary sports game.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трогий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strict, stern').

examples.trans: How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.
examples.trans: We have a very strict principal at our school.

examples.text: Ой, спина не разгибается! Какая вы строгая, Клавдия Викторовна.
examples.trans: Ow, my back won't straighten! How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.

examples.trans: I want him to leave.
She has already gone home.
So should I leave?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'казание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'instruction, direction, order' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The cooks are waiting for the chef's instructions.

examples.text: Лёва очень волнуется без ваших строгих указаний.
examples.trans: Lyova is very anxious without your strict instructions.
Put on a clean apron.

examples.text: А что делать с грязными фартуками?
examples.trans: And what to do with dirty aprons?

examples.text: Я просто принёс чистые поварские фартуки.
examples.trans: I just brought clean chef aprons.

meanings.note: играть в футбол = to play football

examples.trans: Fishing, cars, football.
The boys are playing football.

examples.text: Самсон, ты же опаздываешь на футбол!
examples.trans: Samson, you are late for football!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'station, workshop, section' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Lyova commands the hot station.

examples.text: Иди и проследи за горячим цехом.
examples.trans: Go and supervise the hot kitchen section.

examples.text: Пусть Лёва сам командует на горячем цеху!
examples.trans: Let Lyova command the hot station himself!
The cook peels bananas.
Better keep peeling bananas!

examples.text: Там мне дают только чистить овощи.
examples.trans: There they only give me vegetables to peel.

meanings.note: short form чисто: всё чисто = everything is clean

examples.trans: Everything is clean.
A clean floor.

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.
examples.trans: Nina, I washed everything. It's all clean.
Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
